name: Thane Dyggve

facts.text: Thane Dyggve is a level-66 named with 30,000 health in Dodens Gruva.
He drains energy and summons lightning hammers: Command Mjollnir, 500 damage in a 350 radius.
A May 2003 Allakhazam comment describes him as a big troll with a two-handed hammer in thane epic armour, easy for one group if meleed quickly, and warns his area hammers hurt more than Mjollnir.
In the Ynglinga saga, Dyggvi is a Swedish king who died of sickness rather than in battle (to verify).

story:
Dyggve was Ormarr's thane, a troll of the old frontier, huge and slow and devoted, who wore the harness of a thane of Thor and carried a two-handed hammer he had made himself. When the jarl chose the hill east of Glenlock for his mine, it was Dyggve who swung the first hammer. He did not swing it at the rock. He swung it at the sky, and called down Thor's lightning, and the lightning split the hill open like a log, and the miners cheered, and said the mountain had opened for him like a door. It was the proudest day of his life.

His name is an old one. The kings of the Yngling line, the saga says, had a Dyggvi among them who died in his bed of sickness rather than in battle, a shameful death for a king. Dyggve the thane would not have that. When the cold seam came and the dead began to walk, he stood at the front with the jarl and fought what came up out of the dark, and when the jarl went down to fetch the dead back, Dyggve went with him.

He still fights, in his thane's harness, with the hammer in both hands. He drains the strength from those around him and calls down his lightning hammers, Command Mjollnir, on a whole group at once, hammers that strike harder than any thane's Mjollnir in Jordheim. The lightning answers him yet, but slower and colder than it did, as if it reaches him from very far away, from a sky he can no longer see. The thanes of Midgard who fight him say they feel sorry for him. Then he hits them, and they stop.
legend: Dyggve is one group's work if you melee him fast. Don't let him finish his hammers: interrupt, or the whole group eats 500 each. Old raiders say his hammers hurt more than the real Mjollnir, and they meant it as a warning. Two warriors and a bot did him in 2003; two paladins got him to half. He drains energy too, so long fights go badly. His glowing icebound hammer is the drop thanes want. Stagger the melee so the hammers don't catch everyone, and keep a healer out of the hammer circle at all times. Thanes like to fight him with their own Mjollnir, for the story.

aggro: Thor! Split the rock one more time!
The mountain opened for me once!
death: The thunder... is so far away...
Not in bed... not in bed... in battle...

loremasterTopic.text: Ormarr's thane, a troll who swung the first hammer of the mine and called down lightning to split the rock. The lightning still answers him, slower and colder, as if from far away.

bookPage: From the songs of the Jamtland thanes, as a thane of Jordheim taught them to me. When Ormarr wanted iron, Dyggve called the sky. The sky came down. The hill split. The thanes sing that this was the greatest calling of Thor any troll ever made, and that the god must have been pleased, because he answered at once. The song does not say whether the god was pleased with what was under the hill. The thane who sang it to me stopped there and said that every thane prays, before calling the lightning, that it will not open anything that should stay shut.
